alt: On the left, summary: sources A, B and C reported one after another in the order given, with the writer absent. On the right, synthesis: the writer’s thesis on top, with sources grouped under two ideas and connected by commentary. A test asks whether the argument is still yours if the sources are removed.
caption: In synthesis the writer’s thesis, not the order of the sources, controls the structure.

after: ## Ways to put sources in conversation
alt: Six moves for relating sources to a claim, each with example phrasing: support, extend, qualify, complicate, rebut and compare.
caption: Support, extend, qualify, complicate, rebut, compare: let the relations shape paragraphs.

alt: Four situations and what to do: a direct quotation needs quotation marks and the source’s name; a paraphrase or summary still needs the name; an idea or statistic from a source needs credit; common knowledge needs no citation. Below, three ways to attribute inside a sentence: signal phrase, embedded and parenthetical.
caption: Credit words and ideas that are not yours, in a way that keeps your sentence in charge.

alt: Seven numbered steps zig-zag down the page: decide your position, tag the sources, group them by idea, draft a thesis, build paragraphs around claims, write commentary, and add a counterargument or qualification from a complicating source.
caption: Choose your position first; the sources serve it.

after: ## A public-domain example of conversation with a source: Thoreau (1849)
alt: Thoreau’s sentence, “the true place for a just man is also a prison”, branches two ways: extending it to a standard for protesters who should accept the penalty, or qualifying it for cases where jailing the objector helps the injustice continue.
caption: A brief, attributed quotation becomes a springboard for the writer’s own move.

after: ## Worked example 1: synthesising three invented sources
alt: Two overlapping ovals group the fictional sources: benefits (Source A, unchanged results and better staff retention) and costs (Source B, 58 percent of households facing higher childcare costs).
